rules.effect: Rental units in buildings whose building permit issued after Dec 31, 1975 are EXEMPT from DC rent stabilization (D.C. Code § 42-3502.05(a)(2)); pre-1976 stock is presumptively covered unless another exemption applies. Newly created units in existing structures with a C of O after Jan 1, 1980 are also exempt.
rules.quote: Any rental unit in any newly constructed housing accommodation for which the building permit was issued after December 31, 1975 ... shall be exempt
rules.verification: 3-0 adversarial panel against fetched code text

rules.effect: Pre-1976 building escapes rent stabilization ONLY via the small-landlord exemption: housing accommodation of 4 or fewer rental units (aggregated across structures), owned by not more than 4 natural persons, none holding any direct or indirect interest in any other DC rental unit. An LLC or corporate owner does NOT qualify; owning any other DC rental disqualifies. Claim of exemption must be registered (RAD registration/BBL still required).
rules.quote: (3) ... any rental unit in any housing accommodation of 4 or fewer rental units, including any aggregate of 4 rental units whether within the same structure or not, provided: (A) The housing accommodation is owned by not more than 4 natural persons; (B) None of the housing providers has an interest, either directly or indirectly, in any other rental unit in the District of Columbia
rules.verification: 3-0 adversarial panel against fetched code text

rules.effect: For COVERED accommodations (5+ units; and 2-4 unit buildings majority-owned by a business corporation — see dc-topa-2-4-unit-exemption), sale requires a tenant opportunity to purchase at a bona fide offer (D.C. Code § 42-3404.02(a), as reorganized by D.C. Law 26-80 eff. 2025-12-31). Entity-interest transfers count as a 'sale' (§ 42-3404.02(c)(1)(B)(i) pre-amendment text) — TOPA cannot be structured around for covered buildings. 5+ unit offers without a third-party contract trigger the tenant-organization appraisal regime (§ 42-3404.02(a-1)).
rules.verification: Pre-amendment text quotes from July fetch of code; Law 26-80 reorganization applied per snippet-confirmed law page + firm alerts; post-amendment section text not yet directly fetched

rules.effect: ENACTED: RENTAL Amendment Act of 2025 = D.C. Law 26-80 (Bill B26-0164 -> Act 26-199 signed Nov 13, 2025 -> effective Dec 31, 2025 after congressional review). Amends the Rental Housing Act (expedited eviction review, reduced pre-filing notice periods) and TOPA: exempts SINGLE-FAMILY accommodations (incl. house + one ADU, and a single unit in a condo/co-op/HOA) from TOPA; clarifies 2-4 unit TOPA rules do not apply to 2-unit single-family accommodations; adds a NEW-CONSTRUCTION exemption (sale within 15 years of permanent C of O, applied retroactively to the effective date); preserves the elderly/disabled single-family tenant carve-out (rental agreement signed by 2018-03-31, occupancy by 2018-04-15). A later Council item 'tightens language on prior RENTAL Act passage' — possible follow-up amendment, unreviewed.
rules.verification: Law number, short title, and effective date snippet-confirmed on code.dccouncil.gov page titles; substance via lims.dccouncil.gov engrossment + Ballard Spahr Jan 2026 alert; enacted section text not directly fetchable from this environment — reconfirm before closing on a TOPA-sensitive deal

rules.effect: Under D.C. Law 26-80 (eff. 2025-12-31), 2-4 unit accommodations are EXEMPT from TOPA unless the accommodation is majority-owned by a business CORPORATION ('majority ownership interests' = majority of the value of capital, profits, and losses). Per practitioner analysis, LLC/partnership/trust ownership retains the exemption — only corporate majority ownership re-triggers TOPA. This materially de-risks DC 2-4 unit purchases vs the pre-2026 regime. CAUTION: statutory text not directly fetched; practitioner reading (Federal Title) is the source for the corporation-only nuance — verify the enacted definition before relying on entity structure.
rules.verification: Law existence + long-title TOPA amendments snippet-confirmed on official pages; corporation-ownership nuance from federaltitle.com practitioner alert; single-family definition snippet-confirmed

rules.effect: Vacant property is taxed at Class 3 ($5.00 per $100 assessed) and blighted at Class 4 ($10.00 per $100) vs Class 1 residential $0.85 per $100 — a 6-12x carrying-cost penalty during long renovations unless a vacancy exemption is obtained.
rules.verification: OTR rate table, single primary source

rules.effect: Montgomery County rent stabilization (Bill 15-23, effective 2024) caps annual increases at CPI-U + 3%, maximum 6%. Key exemptions include buildings first occupied fewer than 23 years ago (rolling window) and small owner-occupied configurations; exact exemption list in county code — verify per deal.
rules.verification: Cap formula verified in July 15 pass (CPI+3% capped at 6%); exemption details sourced, panel cut

rules.effect: Takoma Park runs its OWN rent stabilization (City Code Ch. 6.20) on top of being inside Montgomery County: covers all rental properties of 2+ units (and individually rented condos), with NO small-building or natural-person exemption comparable to DC/PG. Allowance = 100% of CPI change; July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027 allowance published at 3.0% (corrected from an initially published 3.3%). Vacancy control reported (cap persists between tenancies) - pending confirmation.
rules.verification: City newsflash + code chapter snippet-confirmed; panels cut by usage limit

rules.effect: Permanent Rent Stabilization and Protection Act (CB-055-2024, amending County Code § 13-147; lineage CB-007-2023 temporary cap -> CB-008-2024 -> CB-055-2024 permanent — NOTE: 'CB-007-2025' is an unrelated employee-benefits bill): annual rent increases for covered units capped at the LESSER of 6.0% or CPI-U + 3% (age-restricted senior facilities: lesser of 4.5% or CPI-U). Annual allowance updates each July 1. Enactment/effective dates CONFLICT across sources (enacted 2024-06-18 / effective 2024-09-15 per county FAQ; passed 2024-07-16, signed 2024-08-01, effective 2024-10-17 per others) — dates unverified pending a direct Legistar pull; the cap itself is consistently stated.
rules.verification: County DPIE pages + CB-55 FAQ PDF (Rev. 5-14-25) concur on the cap formula; effective-date conflict flagged

rules.effect: A rental unit is EXEMPT from the PRSA if the landlord owns 'five (5) or fewer rental units within the County' AND is '(1) a natural person or a living trust of a natural person, or (2) the trust or estate of a decedent' (exact-phrase confirmed). County FAQ states plainly: 'If you own the property through an LLC or corporate entity, the PRSA applies.' DOMICILE FINDING — SETTLED: the domicile-in-county condition attaches ONLY to the separate CONDOMINIUM exemption ('owned by one or more individuals domiciled in the County', expressly tied to § 13-147) and to the owner-occupied original-2-unit exemption; the 5-or-fewer natural-person exemption carries NO domicile condition — a Virginia-resident natural person qualifies. Other § 13-147 exemptions: religious facilities, regulated-affordable units, cooperatives, dormitories, 501(c)(3) temporary-shelter facilities. No exemption application needed while conditions hold ('not considered to be regulated rental units'); exemption lapses when conditions cease.
rules.verification: Exact-phrase snippet confirmation ('five (5) or fewer rental units' + 'natural person') matched both the county HTML FAQ and the CB-55 FAQ PDF (Rev. 5-14-25), plus 3 independently-labeled queries; both documents are DPIE-authored, so a direct § 13-147 code-text pull is still queued before the 'verified' label

rules.effect: Rental dwelling license required for non-owner-occupied rentals including 1-2 family homes (expanded 2018; Baltimore City Code Art. 13). Since Jan 1, 2019 an unlicensed landlord has NO legal right to collect rent. No rent-increase percentage cap exists, but increases are barred while housing-code violation notices citing serious defects remain unabated — directly binding on dated value-add stock; sequence is license, cure violations, then reposition.
rules.verification: Maryland People's Law Library (Maryland State Law Library); snippet-confirmed across independent queries; city code text not directly fetched

rules.effect: No Virginia locality may impose rent control — but the mechanism is Dillon Rule ABSENCE OF GRANT, not an express statutory ban: no Code section grants (or expressly prohibits) locality rent regulation, and localities hold only powers expressly granted or necessarily implied. Enabling bills keep failing (SB 366 defeated in committee; HB 721 continued; HB 278/SB 355 sent to a Virginia Housing Commission 'Local Rent Regulation Authority Bill Study', June 2026, carried toward 2027) — WATCH ITEM: passage of an enabling act would change this row. CITE CORRECTION: § 55.1-1243 (sometimes cited for 'no rent control') is REPEALED (Acts 2021 Sp. Sess. I cc. 403-404, eff. 2021-07-01) and covered tenant ouster remedies, now § 55.1-1243.1 — it was never a rent-control provision. VRLTA statewide terms: security deposit capped — 'No landlord may demand or receive a security deposit, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of two months' periodic rent' (§ 55.1-1226, exact-phrase confirmed); deposit itemization within 45 days of termination/vacancy; § 55.1-1204 governs rental-agreement terms (an amended version takes effect 2027-07-01 — review before then).
rules.verification: Absence-of-grant confirmed by domain-restricted searches of law.lis.virginia.gov (no rent-control section exists in the Code); § 55.1-1226 cap sentence exact-phrase confirmed; failed-bill history via Virginia Mercury + vhc.virginia.gov study PDF

rules.effect: Philadelphia Code § 9-811: before taking steps to evict, a landlord must enroll in the city's Eviction Diversion Program, give the tenant notice of diversion rights, and participate in reasonable good faith for at least 30 days before filing in Municipal Court. Adds a mandatory pre-filing delay to turnover of occupied units. No unit-count carve-out found in operative text (small landlords covered). Pennsylvania has no state or local rent control.
rules.quote: the landlord participates in the eviction diversion program in reasonable good faith, as defined by the City, for no less than thirty (30) days
rules.verification: 3-0 adversarial panel; statute text snippet-confirmed via independent exact-phrase searches

rules.effect: PA 22-30 (2022) made fair rent commissions MANDATORY in every CT municipality of 25,000+ (ordinance deadline July 1, 2023) — New Haven, Hartford, Bridgeport all covered. Under CGS § 7-148b commissions hold adjudicative power: investigate complaints, subpoena, hold hearings, and ORDER rent reductions for rents found harsh and unconscionable. Case-by-case rent regulation risk on post-renovation repositioning. Separately, PA 24-143 §§ 16-17 (eff. Oct 1, 2024) requires 45 days' advance written notice statewide for any rent increase; tenant non-response is not agreement.
rules.verification: OLR report language snippet-confirmed across independent queries; PDF 403-blocked to fetchers; panels cut

rules.effect: ETPA rent stabilization's qualifying vacancy analysis is restricted to buildings of 6+ units built before Jan 1, 1974 — 2-4 unit product sits OUTSIDE ETPA even in municipalities that opt in. Post-2019 HSTPA any NY municipality may opt in on a sub-5% vacancy finding (latent adoption risk), but as of July 16, 2026 HCR lists adoptions only in Nassau, Rockland, Westchester, and Ulster counties — no Capital Region (Albany/Troy) adoption.
rules.verification: HCR page sentences verbatim-confirmed via independent domain-restricted search snippets; panels cut
